nist_cm.source: NIST ASD Rn I levels table (local copy data/nist/Rn_I_levels.tsv)

levels.label: 6p5(2P°3/2)7s 2[3/2]°2
levels.note: metastable lower level of the 745 nm line used for collinear laser spectroscopy (populated by charge exchange of a fast Rn+ beam)

transitions.label: 7s 2[3/2]°2 - 7p 2[5/2]3 (745.0 nm air)
transitions.use: the line of the only laser-spectroscopy study of radon: collinear fast-beam laser spectroscopy at ISOLDE (Borchers, Neugart, Otten et al., Hyperfine Interact. 34, 25 (1987)): isotope shifts between 16 isotopes in the range 202-222Rn and hyperfine structure of 7 odd-A isotopes, per the abstract.
transitions.note: the numerical isotope shifts and A, B constants are not in any source that could be opened; only the abstract was read (https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/6015938)

not_found: isotope shifts and hyperfine A, B constants of the 745 nm line (Borchers et al., Hyperfine Interact. 34, 25 (1987)): papers are behind a paywall, CERN document server blocked automated access; only the abstract and the nuclear moments derived from them (IAEA table) were recovered
radiative lifetimes of any Rn I level (7s, 7p, 6d): no measurement found; no calculated values found either (two web searches, arXiv and INSPIRE queries)
transition probabilities / oscillator strengths of the 178.6 nm and 145.2 nm resonance lines and of the 7s-7p near-infrared lines: none found; NIST ASD lists none
lifetime of the metastable 7s 2[3/2]°2 level: none found
precise (laser) frequencies of any Rn I line: none found; all wavelengths are the classical discharge-spectrum values that NIST uses
measured ionization energy more recent than the NIST value 86692.5 cm^-1: none found
notes: Radon is the least-studied of these atoms: apart from the classical emission spectra there is a single collinear-laser-spectroscopy study (ISOLDE, published 1987) on the 745 nm line, whose numbers could not be opened in this session. Nuclear spins, half-lives and moments are taken from the IAEA table; moments printed there for even-even isotopes belong to isomers and were left out. The site's default isotope (222Rn) has I = 0, so no hyperfine structure applies to it.
